# REDTEAM #144 (SPEC Sec 3.2, T-302): stack slice passed to cgo invalidated.
# A slice make with variable effective capacity that flows into a cgo
# argument or an unsafe.Pointer conversion MUST NOT use the stack buffer
# and MUST allocate its backing storage on the heap. Fixed-effective-capacity
# makes MUST retain ordinary escape and size behavior, not a guarantee of
# stack allocation. Effective capacity is the explicit capacity when present,
# otherwise the length; it is fixed only when the compiler proves it constant
# with ir.IsSmallIntConst after literal rewriting.
#
# This script pins the narrow rule from both sides without touching budgets:
# dynamic-capacity makes flowing to unsafe.Pointer (builtin println sink, no
# other heap edge) and to a real cgo call MUST escape to heap, while a
# fixed-capacity make through the same unsafe sink and a dynamic make with
# only local use MUST stay stack-eligible (no heap line). The println sink
# is a builtin with no heap edge, so the unsafe cases isolate the foreign
# flow; the cgo case proves the backing stays valid across the call.
# Fixed 16 bytes fits the 32-byte default buffer and the 64KB implicit
# limit, so a heap line there would mean the rule was widened beyond
# variable capacity. Budgets (32/256/4096) are unchanged by this gate.

[!cgo] skip
env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local
env CGO_ENABLED=1

# Dynamic unsafe.Pointer case: variable effective capacity (param len, no
# explicit cap) flowing to unsafe.Pointer must escape to heap.
go build -gcflags=-m ./dyn
stderr 'dyn\.go:.*make\(\[\]byte.*escapes to heap'

# Fixed-capacity and local-use controls: no make escapes to heap
# (stack-eligible, budgets preserved). The pattern names the make so the
# incidental panic-string heap line cannot trip it.
go build -gcflags=-m ./fix
! stderr 'make\(\[\]byte.*escapes to heap'

# Dynamic cgo case: variable capacity through a real cgo call must escape
# to heap, and the call must run correctly on the heap backing.
go build -gcflags=-m -o $WORK/cgodyn$GOEXE ./cgodyn
stderr 'cgodyn\.go:.*make\(\[\]byte.*escapes to heap'
go run ./cgodyn
stdout '^cgo ok$'

-- go.mod --
module example.com/redteam144

go 1.27

-- dyn/dyn.go --
package dyn

import "unsafe"

// VarUnsafe passes a variable-capacity slice to unsafe.Pointer through a
// builtin sink with no other heap edge, isolating the foreign flow.
func VarUnsafe(n int) {
	if n <= 0 {
		panic("dyn: n must be positive")
	}
	s := make([]byte, n)
	println(unsafe.Pointer(&s[0]), len(s))
}

-- fix/fix.go --
package fix

import "unsafe"

// FixedUnsafe passes a fixed-capacity slice through the same sink; the
// narrow rule leaves it stack-eligible, so no heap line may appear.
func FixedUnsafe() {
	s := make([]byte, 16, 16)
	println(unsafe.Pointer(&s[0]), len(s), cap(s))
}

// VarLocal uses a variable-capacity make with only local use; ordinary
// size behavior keeps it stack-eligible, so no heap line may appear.
func VarLocal(n int) int {
	if n <= 0 {
		panic("fix: n must be positive")
	}
	s := make([]byte, n)
	sum := 0
	for _, v := range s {
		sum += int(v)
	}
	return sum + len(s)
}

-- cgodyn/cgodyn.go --
package main

/*
#include <stddef.h>
int r144fill(char *p, int n) {
	for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) p[i] = (char)(i & 0x7f);
	return n;
}
*/
import "C"

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"unsafe"
)

//go:noinline
func fill(n int) {
	s := make([]byte, n)
	C.r144fill((*C.char)(unsafe.Pointer(&s[0])), C.int(n))
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		if s[i] != byte(i&0x7f) {
			panic("redteam144: cgo-filled slice corrupted")
		}
	}
}

func main() {
	n := 64 + len(os.Args)%2
	fill(n)
	fmt.Println("cgo ok")
}
